root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: `p->decoders` must remain caller-owned on the `ret == -1` create-time error path; the cleanup there must not release it through `flb_parser_destroy(p)`.
root_cause_criterion.criterion: When `flb_parser_create()` is about to return `NULL` from the `time_offset` failure path, it must preserve the caller-owned decoder list still stored in `p->decoders` and leave the later harness cleanup as the first destroy of that list.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original violates this ownership-preservation obligation by routing the create-time failure path through `flb_parser_destroy(p)`, which frees `p->decoders` before parser creation succeeds. The fixed original keeps the same decoder-list pointer live by using `flb_interim_parser_destroy(p)`, so the caller-side failure cleanup performs the first and only decoder-list destroy.

nodes.state: The second `flb_parser_decoder_list_destroy(list)` reaches `mk_list_foreach_safe(head, tmp, list)` with the same decoder-list head pointer; in the vulnerable run that head was already freed during create-time cleanup, so the macro reads stale list links and triggers the AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free READ.

Because `flb_parser_create()` returned `NULL`, the harness failure-cleanup branch still calls `flb_parser_decoder_list_destroy(list)` with the same decoder-list pointer it allocated earlier. In the vulnerable run that pointer has already been released by create-time parser cleanup.

edges.relation: The same decoder-list pointer still stored in `p->decoders` on the create-time failure path later remains in the caller's `list` variable, so the harness cleanup re-enters decoder-list destroy on that pointer after parser creation returned `NULL`.

The harness failure-cleanup call forwards that same stale `list` pointer into `flb_parser_decoder_list_destroy()` as its `list` parameter, carrying the freed decoder-list head directly into the crashing `mk_list_foreach_safe` iteration.
